summary.intent: Assess whether Phase 72 needed discussion before planning, retire stale/addressed todos and fold new ones into Phase 72/73 scope, then run the full plan→execute→ship flow for Phase 72 (with 73 to follow) — but the session was hijacked by an urgent CI fire (web-e2e and desktop-e2e failures) that had to be root-caused and fixed before returning to Phase 72 planning.
summary.outcome: Fixed three real CI regressions traced to Phase 70.1/71 fallout across PRs #601 (merged: FUSE seq-1 equivocation fix, stale desktop-e2e DTO field driver, greptile perf optimization) and #600 (merged: rotation-floor store fix, sdk-e2e Test 21 idempotency fix, plus 4 web-e2e flake source-fixes for tests 4.10/4.11/6.6.2/8.2), validated both via CI-equivalent local runs and dispatched workflow runs, then resumed and completed Phase 72 planning (research → pattern-mapping → 10 plans across 8 waves, all committed) with 8 retired Phase 71 todos and ROADMAP updates folded into the planning commit.

repo: GSD repo closes todos by deleting them from pending/ and adding them to completed/ — an empty resolved/ folder is a red herring; check completed/ instead

Phase 71 (#599) shipped without retiring its 8 source todos from pending/, and separately left three pieces of test/fixture drift unfixed (stale desktop-e2e .mts DTO field names, an sdk-e2e Test 21 assertion that didn't account for its own idempotency, and exposed a latent FUSE seq-1 equivocation bug) — a systemic pattern worth flagging in ship retrospectives

ci-e2e.yml (Web E2E + Desktop E2E) triggers ONLY on push-to-main or workflow_dispatch, never on pull_request — PR checks give no e2e signal; must dispatch manually via `gh workflow run <file> --ref <branch>` (not `-f ref=`, which 422s on workflows predating that input) to validate before merging

web-e2e Playwright ciFloor() helper raises wait timeouts to a 60s floor only under CI (process.env.CI) — local runs use much tighter timeouts (15-30s), causing local-only flakes on IPNS-gated mutations (delete/restore/mkdir) that pass fine in CI; representative local verification requires CI=1, which also flips webServer.reuseExistingServer to false and fights an already-running dev stack

packages/sdk/src/client.ts is the real dependency coupling between Phase 72 and Phase 73 — 72 rewrites write-plane primitives (getWriteBodyParams, helper dedup) that 73's SC#3/#4 build directly on top of; sequencing 72→73 is required, though 73's SC#1/#2/#5 (pure apps/web, e.g. useSharedNavigationActions.ts, SharedFolderRow.tsx) are independent and could run in parallel

GSD hook JSON files (plan:pre capability fragments) contain raw/literal control characters inside string values, making them non-strict-JSON — direct JSON.parse and jq --raw both fail; requires a custom lenient parser that escapes control chars only inside string literals

Rust FUSE fix pattern: for a per-file first-publish path guarded by 'is inode cid empty', a stale/dropped UploadComplete retry can re-trigger a hardcoded seq=1 publish; correct fix is to resolve the IPNS name first (mirroring resolve_ipns_for_replay in replay.rs) and route to the existing CAS-retry path (with an optional preresolved_seq to skip a redundant second resolve) rather than skip entirely, since content may have genuinely changed

code.finding: publish_file_node hardcoded seq=1 on first-publish branch gated only by 'inode cid empty' — didn't handle a stale UploadComplete retry re-publishing genuinely-changed content, which the Phase 71 anti-equivocation gate then rejected as equivocation

publish_with_cas_retry is the shared CAS helper for both file and folder(bin) publish paths; added optional preresolved_seq param so a caller that already resolved the sequence (e.g. via the Found guard) skips a redundant second resolve on the first attempt — conflict-retry path always re-resolves since pre-resolved values go stale after a conflict

Test 4.10 'Batch delete via action bar' uses a 15s local waitForItemToDisappear wait that reliably exceeds on this hardware for IPNS-gated batch deletes; bumped to 30s (CI still floors to 60s via ciFloor, so no CI behavior change) — same class of fix applied to 4.11 batch move

Test 6.6.2 restore-version assertion used a no-op gate (getVersionCount()===1, true both before and after a restore swap) providing zero wait for the IPNS republish, then read the editor content once — inherently racy; replaced with expect.poll of the actual editor content

ciFloor() helper raises wait timeouts to 60s only when process.env.CI is set — local runs use the caller's literal timeout, creating a systematic local/CI asymmetry that causes local-only flakes on IPNS-gated mutation waits

workflow: When multiple background local test runs are needed to isolate flakes/cascades, iterate with warm-stack re-runs before assuming ambient degradation — but if flakes keep surfacing at different points in a serial suite, switch to running under the CI-equivalent timeout regime (CI=1) rather than continuing whack-a-mole source-fixes against a systematically tighter local timeout budget

When a CI workflow's dispatch forces both a web and a desktop job together, check whether the branch under test actually contains upstream fixes (e.g. from a sibling PR) before dispatching — rebase first if not, to avoid a false-negative failure on stale code
Before pushing a rebased/force-pushed branch, re-fetch and check for an intervening bot commit (e.g. chore(release)) so force-push-with-lease doesn't clobber it
Greptile P2 (optional, non-blocking) comments are worth fixing immediately if the fix is small/contained even after being initially deferred as low-value — re-evaluate scope before declining

Temporarily patching a config file (e.g. playwright.config.ts webServer.reuseExistingServer) for local verification purposes is fine if the exact change is tracked and reverted immediately after use, confirmed via diff showing no residual change

friction: Repeated local test runs (7 separate background runs) needed to actually exercise the target fixed tests (6.6.2, 8.2), because a chain of unrelated local-only flakes (4.10, 4.11, 2.1 create-folder) kept cascading and blocking downstream tests from ever executing — significant time sunk before landing on the CI=1 regime as the representative verification method
CI=1 locally conflicts with webServer.reuseExistingServer (`!process.env.CI`), forcing a temporary config patch to get a CI-equivalent run against an already-running dev stack

GSD hook JSON files are not strict JSON (raw control characters in string values) — jq --raw and JSON.parse both failed, requiring a custom lenient parser script; ultimately partial (had to author a research prompt manually rather than fully extracting the hook fragment)
`gh workflow run -f ref=` returned a 422 'Unexpected inputs' because main's workflow definition predated that input — had to discover `--ref <branch>` as the working alternative
git commit hung for 2 minutes due to a likely 1Password SSH signing prompt during lint-staged, requiring a manual check of whether the commit actually landed before retrying

Confusing/contradictory `cat-file` output when verifying whether the 8 todo `completed/` counterparts were in HEAD — required a second decisive check to resolve what turned out to be a buggy earlier check, not an actual state problem
